newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Australia-Asia ties hurt by Hanson, report -Beazle.
newsitem.headline: Australia-Asia ties hurt by Hanson, report -Beazle.

text.p: A leaked government report critical of South Pacific leaders and the race row sparked by Pauline Hanson have "poisoned the well" of Australia's good Asian relations, opposition leader Kim Beazley said on Tuesday.
"There is no aspect of what is an increasingly seamless interconnection with Asian life and Australian life that is not in some way harmed by this," Beazley told reporters.

"It's poisoned the well in our relationships with nations in the South Pacific," Labor Party leader Beazley said after a speech to the Singapore Foreign Correspondents Association in which he stressed his belief Australia had a role to play at the heart of Asian society.
Two AUSTEO (Australian Eyes Only) papers were left on a table in a public area at a recent conference of Pacific economic ministers.

One paper was scathing about South Pacific economies and the foibles of some ministers. The second was a confidential briefing paper to Treasurer Peter Costello ahead of bilateral talks with Pacific economic ministers.

Beazley said there was a danger of a perception developing in Asia that mainstream politicians shared similar views to Hanson, who sparked a row after saying Australia risked being swamped by Asians and called for an immigration freeze.

"It feeds into a business context, it feeds into people's sense of security in coming to Australia, and it feeds into the general intelligence of the region when it comes to any particular set of affairs that they want to conduct with Australia or in fact are conducting with Australia," he said.

He said Australia's relations with Asia were now so finely balanced that the leaked criticisms required an apology that was "a clear cut indication that they do not represent Australian attitudes diplomatically or policy wise".
Beazley was speaking at the end of a week-long global tour. In Singapore he met with Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence Tony Tan.
